references.text: The same question from children about the meaning of Passover, and the command to explain the Lord's deliverance from Egypt
Parallel text in the same chapter about telling your son what the Lord did when he brought the people out of Egypt
The same pattern with the child's question and the parents' answer about the deliverance from Egypt with a strong hand
Reference to the house of bondage in Egypt from which Israel was brought out
The Lord's promise to bring Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand
The command to teach future generations what they have seen
Deliverance from the house of bondage with a strong hand
God's prophecy about striking Egypt with a strong hand
A similar command to explain the stones at the Jordan to children as a reminder of the Lord's work
Children's questions about the meaning of the stones and the explanation of God's mighty works
The command to tell future generations about the Lord's deeds and wonders
Direct parallel in the law regarding parents' duty to convey the exodus from Egypt when children ask
Complementary verse in the same chapter that expands on the purpose of telling children about the exodus
Connected text in the same chapter establishing the historical basis for the command to teach children
Theological parallel where the exodus with a 'strong hand' is used as a foundation for national prayer and identity in exile
Liturgical parallel where the same formula about a 'strong hand' is used in an official confession at the bringing of the first fruits.
